stemMd: What is a principal digestive role of bile salts in the small intestine?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Emulsifying fats to increase the surface available to lipase

options.label: B
options.textMd: Converting starch directly into amino acids

options.label: E
options.textMd: Making the intestine completely impermeable to nutrients

explanationMd: Bile salts disperse large lipid droplets into smaller ones. Increased surface area helps lipase act; emulsification is a physical aid rather than enzymatic cleavage by bile salts themselves.

distractorRationale.b: Starch is a carbohydrate and cannot supply amino-acid identity this way.
distractorRationale.d: Bile salts are not protease enzymes.
distractorRationale.c: Blood-cell formation is unrelated to bile emulsification.
